'''Alex Alcalde''' was a Decipher-era [[Squadron Members|Squadron Member]], listed as Gold 31 from Terre Haute, IN.<ref name="sm-fan" /> The published fan table marks the slot Retired after Decipher's SWCCG run.

A History graduate student at Indiana State University, formerly of Toronto, he started playing in January 1996. In May 1997 he led two carloads of Toronto players to the Rochester Open. In Terre Haute he built a group of about 40 players and a regional website, the [[Corellian Engineering Corporation (fan site)|Corellian Engineering Corporation]]. His motto: "When both Luck and Skill fail you, kick over the table."<ref name="decsq-prof" />

He joined [[Radio Free Decipher]] broadcast 9 (26 February 1999) for a squadron and ambassador call-in with Chris Swearingen, [[Carl Mike Hardy|Mike Hardy]] and [[Guy Kargl]].<ref name="rfd-09">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QU24jFxZsHM Radio Free Decipher 09], Player's Council (26 February 1999). Guests Chris Swearingen, [[Alex Alcalde]], Mike Hardy, and [[Guy Kargl]]. Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-QU24jFxZsHM Internet Archive].</ref>

He made rulings at the [[1998 Corellia Regional (Indianapolis)]] and posted the tournament report.<ref name="list-53912" /> He posted two [[Young Jedi]] lists on the [[Corellian Engineering Corporation (fan site)]] as '''Gold 31''': ''Wizards!'' (Jedi) and ''All Droids All the time!'' (Sith).

== In their own words ==

<blockquote>
Who is Alex?

 Alex is a Graduate student in History at Indiana State University in Terre Haute, Indiana, formerly of Toronto, Canada (that great snow covered land to the North).

 I initially got interested in Star Wars CCG about January of 1996, just pickin' up a starter and a few boosters, as I had just recently sold off all of my Magic Gear and was looking for a cool game.

With tourneys and demos, I had my weekends fairly full, and rarely got to play, but come May '97, I gathered up 2 car loads of daring Torontonians and we set our sights on the Rochester Open. We Came and Conquered ;-)

However, my tenure in Toronto didn't last, as I went elsewhere for graduate school, the only thing I take more seriously than Star Wars
CCG. Currently, I'm enrolled in the Masters program at Indiana State University, and I'm trying to complete my degree by May '00. And for those that will ask, no, I'm not writing a thesis on the history of Star Wars. No, that will come at the Phd level :)

With my recent move to Terre Haute, I brought my Squadron membership with me. Yeah!!! I have started out again, almost like a new SM, building from the ground up. It's sometimes rather tedious, but definitely is
easier the second time round. With the aid of one of my players, I have a Webpage dedicated to Star Wars CCG in Corellia...otherwise known as
the Corellian Engineering Corporation (always under construction) and a SWCCG
Mailing list to all gamers in that area.

 I have built a core group of about 40 players in the Terre Haute region (and growing--with lots of beginners). A recent beginners tourney showed me that there are some really good players that just need a bit of encouragement.

Don't worry Hoosiers, I'm gonna be on for another year here (school year at least) then it might be off to parts unknown. Maybe I'll be coming to a town near you..scarey, eh? (There goes my Canadian side--again)

And remember......"When both Luck and Skill fail you, kick over the table."<ref name="decsq-prof" />
</blockquote>
